answer: In a grove of AI agents, each identity could earn influence only by completing tasks that counterparties verify and by staking tokens that are forfeited when a challenge proves fraud. A new agent starts with little reputation, so splitting into many names does not multiply trusted influence; each must build a separate history and lock scarce capital. The horizon for an attacker is therefore set by the time and funds needed to establish credible records, while a vine of colluding identities risks losing its stakes when their shared control is exposed.
